question: Which of the following is the headquarters of the South Central Zone of Indian Railways?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Secunderabad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The South Central Railway (SCR) zone of Indian Railways is headquartered at **Secunderabad** in Telangana.
 
• Secunderabad is one of the major railway stations and serves as a central hub for rail traffic in the region.
 
• South Central Railway was formed on October 2, 1966, with its headquarters at Secunderabad.
 
• SCR zone covers the states of Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, and parts of Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Railways Zones**

 
 
• Indian Railways is divided into 18 zones, each headed by a General Manager.
 
• Each zone is further divided into divisions, with a Divisional Railway Manager overseeing operations.
 
• The zones were created for better management and operational efficiency of the extensive railway network in India.
 
 
 
• **Secunderabad Railway Station**
 
 
• Secunderabad Junction is one of the oldest railway stations in India, established in 1874.
 
• It is an important station in the South Central Railway zone, with over 190 trains originating or passing through it daily.
 
• The station is well-equipped with modern amenities and facilities for passengers.
 
 
 
• **Formation of South Central Railway**
 
 
• South Central Railway was formed by carving out the Vijayawada and Hubli Divisions from Southern Railway and the Sholapur Division from Central Railway.
 
• SCR aims to enhance the rail connectivity and services in the southern and central parts of India.
 
 
 
• **Major Divisions under SCR**
 
 
• SCR comprises six divisions: Secunderabad, Hyderabad, Vijayawada, Guntakal, Guntur, and Nanded.
 
• Each division is strategically important, catering to both passenger and freight traffic.
